Docs/Scene evaluation

Scene evaluation

Evaluate a frozen policy across the three native kitchen scenes using one shared environment factory.

The fixed three-scene matrix

The default cross-scene track covers all 30 canonical stages on three named native kitchen backgrounds, for 90 task/background pairs. Freeze the learned policy and keep episode seeds and policy inputs consistent across the comparison.

Background IDNative surface
robocasa_l3_s2Blue kitchen stone island
robocasa_l3_s1Light wood kitchen island
robocasa_l3_s6Warm wood kitchen stone island

labutopia_lab003 is available for additional laboratory studies. It is optional and does not belong to the default three-kitchen matrix.

Use the shared factory

Research checkout required

The module examples on this page require an asset-complete research checkout, its compatible Python environment, and the relevant simulator or model dependencies. The current public repository ↗ contains a README, license and repository metadata; cloning it does not provide the task modules, robot assets, datasets or checkpoints used below. These examples document the verified research interfaces.

from utils.dex_scene_eval import BACKGROUND_IDS, make_scene_eval_env

env = make_scene_eval_env(
    "SharpaAngledClickMouse-v1",
    scene_background=BACKGROUND_IDS[0],
    obs_mode="rgb",  # Use "state" for a state-based policy.
)
try:
    obs, info = env.reset(seed=10001)
    background_manifest = env.unwrapped.eval_background_manifest
    # Continue with the frozen policy's observation/action adapter.
    # Save background_manifest with the episode results.
finally:
    env.close()

The factory accepts the 30 canonical subtasks. It enforces one CPU-physics environment, the registered robot and horizon, pd_joint_pos, reset-time reconfiguration and fixed 256 × 256 base/wrist policy cameras. Conflicting overrides raise an error.

Understand what the scene changes

The factory uses the native room's unscaled table and authored collision geometry. The original workspace table and ground have rendering and collisions disabled. At reset, the room is translated to align the robot-facing visible working edge with the original task table; the task's robot root, joint reset and object placements remain those of the task.

A tabletop-height check rejects differences above 1 mm. This alignment does not make the tables physically identical: their dimensions and collision shapes can differ. Save eval_background_manifest, including its geometry and camera information, when reporting transfer results.

Plan the matrix before running a policy

python utils/scene_matrix.py plan --out output/scene90
python utils/scene_matrix.py preview --index 2 --out output/scene90/preview

The preview saves policy-camera frames, diagnostic views and placement checks without loading a learned checkpoint. It requires the same project and scene assets plus a working renderer. A passed placement preview verifies scene construction, not policy success.

Assign disjoint task/background/seed tuples to separate processes; see Parallel environments. Average stage success within each scene, then report mean and standard deviation across scene averages. See aggregation details. Optional procedural training variation is documented under Domain randomization.
